quizzes.name: The Bronze Age Aegean

questions.q: Which script was used to write the earliest known form of Greek?
questions.explain: Linear B was adapted from Minoan Linear A to write Greek. Michael Ventris deciphered it in 1952, pushing attested Greek back roughly five centuries before Homer.

questions.q: What is the strongest evidence that Mycenaean Greeks controlled Knossos after c. 1450 BC?
options: The palace was rebuilt in mainland style
The Knossos archives switch to Linear B, which records Greek
Homer says so in the Iliad
questions.explain: Material culture can travel through trade. Administration cannot: if the palace records are kept in Greek, Greek-speakers were running the palace.

questions.q: Why do Linear B tablets survive at all?
options: They were fired deliberately for permanent storage
Destruction fires baked the unfired clay
They were sealed in dry tombs
questions.explain: The tablets were temporary records meant to be recycled annually. Every archive we have exists because a palace burned down — a striking case of survival bias.

questions.q: The Mask of Agamemnon dates to approximately:
questions.explain: Roughly three centuries before any traditional date for the Trojan War. Schliemann's name for it was wishful, and it has proved impossible to dislodge.

questions.q: Which is NOT supported by current evidence about the Theran eruption?
options: It buried the town of Akrotiri
It generated tsunamis that struck Crete
It directly caused the destruction of the Cretan palaces in 1450 BC
Its ash has been identified across the eastern Mediterranean
questions.explain: On the high chronology the eruption is c. 1620–1600 BC — more than a century before the 1450 BC destructions. The two events cannot be directly linked.

questions.q: What do the late Mycenaean water systems at Mycenae, Tiryns and Athens suggest?
options: A prolonged drought was already underway
questions.explain: Three separate citadels independently cut concealed passages to springs outside their walls, late in the period. That is siege preparation.

quizzes.summary: Minoans, Mycenaeans, and the collapse that ended both.

quizzes.name: Evidence and Confidence

questions.q: A claim resting on an inscription carved in stone is classified as:
questions.explain: Epigraphic evidence is text inscribed on durable material. It is often contemporary with the events, which makes it unusually valuable.

questions.q: Coin hoards are especially useful to historians because they:
options: Always name the ruler who issued them
Provide precise dating and show trade circulation
questions.explain: Numismatic evidence dates deposits tightly and maps economic reach. Athenian owls turning up in Egypt tells you about trade no text records.

questions.q: Which confidence level fits "Agamemnon ruled Mycenae"?
questions.explain: The claim comes solely from poetic tradition with no supporting contemporary evidence. Legendary is not a synonym for false — it marks the kind of claim it is.

questions.q: Which confidence level fits "The Parthenon was built between 447 and 432 BC"?
questions.explain: Inscribed building accounts survive recording expenditure year by year. This is about as securely dated as anything in Greek history.

questions.q: Why is "the Library of Alexandria burned down in one catastrophe" classified as debated?
options: No ancient source mentions the Library
Evidence points to gradual decline through several causes
The Library has never been located
The claim originates in the 19th century
questions.explain: Caesar's harbour fire, lost patronage and the expulsion of scholars all contributed over centuries. The single-catastrophe story is tidier than the evidence.

questions.q: A Minoan fresco reconstructed from a few original fragments should be treated as:
options: Direct archaeological evidence for what Minoans depicted
Partly archaeological evidence, partly modern interpretation
questions.explain: The surviving fragments are evidence. The connecting passages are a modern painter's hypothesis, and the two need to be visually distinguishable.

quizzes.summary: How historians classify what they know — and how sure they are entitled to be.

quizzes.name: Classical Greece

questions.q: Cleisthenes' ten tribes were each composed of trittyes drawn from three different regions in order to:
options: Break the link between aristocratic families and local power bases
questions.explain: A tribe with members from city, coast and inland had no single local patron. It is social engineering as constitutional design.

questions.q: What did Themistocles persuade Athens to do with the silver strike at Laurion in 483 BC?
questions.explain: Three years later that fleet fought at Salamis. It also made the poorest citizens, who rowed the ships, politically indispensable.

questions.q: At Salamis the Greeks fought in narrow straits because:
options: It negated the Persian numerical advantage
The Greek ships were faster in open water
questions.explain: In the narrows a larger fleet cannot deploy and ships foul each other. Themistocles reportedly leaked false intelligence to force the engagement there.

questions.q: Moving the Delian League treasury to Athens in 454 BC mattered because:
options: It marked the conversion of an alliance into an empire
Athens needed the silver for coinage
The temple on Delos had burned
questions.explain: Allied tribute then funded the Acropolis building programme. Members who tried to leave were besieged and forced back.

questions.q: Epaminondas defeated Sparta at Leuctra by:
options: Using cavalry to outflank the phalanx
Massing his left wing fifty ranks deep against the Spartan right
questions.explain: It inverted the convention that the best troops go on the right. Around 400 of 700 Spartiates died — a loss Sparta's demography could not absorb.

questions.q: Which best describes the political context of Socrates' trial?
options: Athens was at the height of its imperial power
Athens had recently lost the war and endured the Thirty Tyrants
Macedon had just taken control of Athens
A plague was ravaging the city
questions.explain: Several of his associates had been prominent in the oligarchy. An amnesty barred prosecuting them for it — but not this.

quizzes.summary: Persian Wars, Athenian democracy, and the war that ended it.

quizzes.name: Myth and History

questions.q: Which of these is NOT narrated in the Iliad?
options: The quarrel between Achilles and Agamemnon
The wooden horse and the fall of Troy
questions.explain: The Iliad covers about fifty days in the tenth year and ends with Hector's funeral. The horse comes from the lost Iliupersis and, in full, from Virgil.

questions.q: What has never been found in Minoan art?
questions.explain: The Minotaur is a Greek story about Crete, not a Minoan one. Bulls are everywhere in Minoan art; the hybrid monster is not.

questions.q: Hittite archives support a historical Troy connection by naming:
options: Wilusa, a king Alaksandu, and a power called Ahhiyawa
A ten-year siege of a coastal city
questions.explain: Independent, contemporary, non-Greek documents naming a place and a power. That is evidence for a context, not for the Iliad's war.

questions.q: Poseidon's importance in the Linear B tablets from Pylos is notable because:
options: He receives more offerings than any other deity, including Zeus
He is not mentioned at all
He appears only as a place name
questions.explain: The Bronze Age pantheon was not the Homeric one. Poseidon was pre-eminent at Pylos and was later demoted as the palace states disappeared.

questions.q: Helen received cult worship at Sparta, which suggests:
options: She was certainly a historical queen
She may have originated as a goddess later demoted to a heroine
The cult was invented in the Hellenistic period
questions.explain: Cult worship is a different kind of evidence from epic narrative, and it points the opposite way from the usual assumption that heroes get promoted.

quizzes.summary: Distinguishing what the stories say from what the evidence shows.

quizzes.name: Alexander and After

questions.q: Philip II's key military innovation was:
options: The sarissa phalanx paired with Companion cavalry
questions.explain: The pike phalanx pins the enemy line while heavy cavalry breaks it at an angle — the hammer-and-anvil system Alexander inherited intact.

questions.q: How is the date of Gaugamela known so precisely?
options: A Babylonian astronomical diary records a lunar eclipse eleven days earlier
Coins struck to commemorate the battle
questions.explain: Astronomical records convert to modern dates exactly. It is one of the most securely dated events in ancient history: 1 October 331 BC.

questions.q: Why did Alexander besiege Tyre for seven months rather than bypass it?
options: He could not leave a Persian naval base behind him
It was the birthplace of Darius III
The oracle at Siwa instructed him to
questions.explain: Strategy, not spite. He built a causeway out to the island, which silted up and permanently joined Tyre to the mainland.

questions.q: What did Seleucus obtain from Chandragupta Maurya, and what did it decide?
options: 500 war elephants; the battle of Ipsus
Iron for weapons; the battle of Gaza
A marriage alliance; the siege of Rhodes
Grain shipments; the battle of Pydna
questions.explain: He traded the easternmost provinces for elephants. At Ipsus they screened Demetrius' cavalry out of the battle, and Antigonus was killed unsupported.

questions.q: The Antikythera mechanism is remarkable chiefly because:
options: It bears an inscription naming Archimedes
It uses bronze gearing to model astronomical cycles, unmatched for over a millennium
questions.explain: At least thirty gears, an eclipse dial, and a pin-and-slot device reproducing the Moon's variable speed. Nothing comparable survives for about 1,400 years.

questions.q: Why did the Roman legion defeat the Macedonian phalanx?
options: Tactical flexibility on broken ground where the phalanx line fragmented
questions.explain: Polybius set out the analysis: the phalanx is unbeatable frontally on level ground, and helpless once gaps open. Maniples were trained to exploit exactly that.

quizzes.summary: The conquest of Persia and the world it produced.
